notes: "The group of names to compare this one against" was being built in several places, each its own way. The comps table resolved it through the peer cohort. Base rates, though, kept a *second* builder: it called the provider peer endpoint and then screened the universe for a sector-and-size band of its own. Two code paths for one idea — which meant the base-rate distribution, the fade curves and the implied-expectations reference could be measured against a *different* peer group than the comps table and the price decomposition were using. Nothing warned you; the numbers just quietly disagreed.
